clue.text: Racialists, vandalising 'phone boxes…

indicators.note: vandalising means smashing up, so the letters of these two words are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Racists are trashing telephone kiosks, and the story continues into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalising' rearranges the letters of PHONE BOXES. The dots link this clue to 6 across, whose surface carries on the story.
explanation.definitionFit: People who hate foreigners are a close cousin of racists, the sense used here.

clue.text: Picture from established artist hung between two unknowns

indicators.note: hung between says the artist is placed between the two letters, like a painting on a wall

parts.note: x and y are the usual unknowns in algebra
the second algebraic unknown
RA, Royal Academician, is an established artist

explanation.surface: A painting by an eminent artist displayed between two anonymous works.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiograph is an image taken of the inside of the body.

clue.text: Pay attention to me, say

explanation.surface: Someone demanding attention for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is mi, a note of the sol-fa scale, not the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed something is to mark it; mi in the tonic sol-fa scale is a musical tone.

clue.text: Forecast about the French bias

indicators.note: about says the forecast word goes around the French article

parts.note: a forecast is a prediction
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A forecast concerning French prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: A partiality or preference for something is a bias towards it.

clue.text: Some microbes enjoy fat

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some germs relish fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Grossly overweight is a stronger word for fat.

clue.text: Try to stop talking all the time

parts.note: to stop something is to end it

indicators.note: talking says the word for all the time is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: ever means always, all the time

explanation.surface: A plea to a chatterbox to stop talking constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling differs from the sound: only the ear hears 'ever' in the closing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt or effort is a try.

clue.text: … left off to lower a boat

indicators.note: off says the letter for the word left is taken away from what remains

parts.note: to lower (rhymes with flower) is to frown or glower, as does a scowl

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across: the vandals leave the phone boxes and go off to launch a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' is not 'let down' but the verb meaning to look sullen. 'off' removes L (left) from SCOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed barge used for carrying cargo is a kind of boat.

clue.text: In olden days you might be found en route for the Old Bailey, perhaps

indicators.note: en is French for in, so the old pronoun is put in the route word

parts.note: a route is a course
thou is the archaic word for you

explanation.surface: In days gone by you might have been met on the way to London's criminal court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bailey is London's Central Criminal Court; 'en' is French for 'in', acting as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Central Criminal Court is a building where trials are heard.

clue.text: Gauge matter we're resolving

indicators.note: resolving here means breaking down into parts, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A meter reading something you think matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolving' rearranges MATTER WERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A device measuring household water supply is a kind of meter.

clue.text: Poised for action in exchange for cash

explanation.surface: Someone stands ready to act, but only if they are paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for cash, so the second reading is literally paying with ready money.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepared to act immediately is the idiom's usual sense; 'the ready' is slang for money, so the phrase can also mean paid in coin.

clue.text: A pound as kickback

explanation.surface: A pound handed over as a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: The punt was the Irish pound. 'Kickback' wants to be a bribe, but read as a kick that sends the ball back downfield.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish currency unit before the euro, and a kick from the hands that drives the ball back towards the opposition.

clue.text: Sound — pretend to be otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone healthy faking illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors sounded depth by swinging a lead weight on a line; the phrase is also British slang for malingering.
explanation.definitionFit: Measuring water depth with a weighted line, and shirking by faking illness, when one is in fact healthy.

clue.text: Soft drink for a digger convert out of W. Australia

parts.note: a digger who works underground for coal is a miner

indicators.note: out of here says the word for convert sits outside the abbreviation

parts.note: to convert something is to alter it
WA is the abbreviation for Western Australia

explanation.surface: Recommending a non-alcoholic drink to an Australian, a digger, who wants to change his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digger' suggests an Australian soldier, fitting W. Australia, but it is a miner.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottled spring water, sparkling or still, is sold as a non-alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Disposing of papa's medal causes a lump in one's throat

indicators.note: disposing in its sense of arranging means the letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Getting rid of father's medal makes someone emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lump in one's throat' wants to be emotion, but is the literal bump of the larynx; 'Disposing of' rearranges PAPAS MEDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The visible bulge of the larynx at the front of the neck is a literal lump there.

clue.text: When board takes people initially to task

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left
a board with lettering is a sign
men are people

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of the word to

explanation.surface: A committee gets people to account at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a committee but is a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work allotted to someone is a task.

clue.text: Hooligan giving educationalists a bit of trouble

parts.note: DES was the Department of Education and Science, the British education ministry
a, as in so much a head, means per
ado is fuss or a bit of trouble

explanation.surface: A thug gives teachers some grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is used in the sense 'per', as in 'ten pence a go'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless outlaw or ruffian is close enough to a lawless thug.

clue.text: In love soldiers abandon pretence

indicators.note: abandon says the soldiers leave the word for pretence

parts.note: affectation is a pretence or put-on manner
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers in love drop their pretence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandon' removes TA from AFFECTATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondness or warm attachment is a mild form of love.

clue.text: Sorrowful lady, one dressed in black, returning

indicators.note: returning says the whole built word is read back to front
dressed in says the numeral one is clothed by the colour word

parts.note: ebon is a poetic word for black
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mourning woman in black clothes, going home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed in' puts I inside EBON to make EBOIN; 'returning' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this queen wept endlessly for her slain children and was turned to weeping stone.

clue.text: Second, as well as first, rainy

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second
1st, with the 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Something placed second and first at once, then the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1ST, with the figure 1 standing for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp weather, as on a drizzly day, is wet but not pouring.

clue.text: Anticipate a warning smack

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout
a smack is a taste or flavour, as in a smack of garlic

explanation.surface: Someone braces for a slap after being warned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like a blow, but it means a flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample in advance is to expect or get a glimpse of what is to come.

clue.text: Queen in a novel fences badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters of these three words are put together in poor order

explanation.surface: A queen in a book makes a poor job of sword fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges A NOVEL FENCES. She was Henry VIII's fourth wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's fourth wife was a royal consort of England.

clue.text: Record books always around

indicators.note: around says the poetic always goes about the books

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Books that keep records forever.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is the poetic contraction of ever, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To write an item into a ledger is to record it.

clue.text: A heartless, unprincipled person

parts.note: describes a debauched rake; heartless also hints that a five-letter rascal loses its middle letter

explanation.surface: A description of a cold scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the heart (G) out of ROGUE and you get this rake, who is himself heartless and unprincipled.
explanation.definitionFit: A debauched man of loose morals is a callous rake.

clue.text: Take-off in second gear

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: An aircraft taking off in second gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take-off' looks like an aircraft leaving, but means a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic sketch parodying someone is a send-up.

clue.text: Look, but hold back

indicators.note: back says the word for hold is read in reverse

parts.note: to keep is to hold

explanation.surface: An instruction to look but restrain yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns KEEP round.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick furtive glance is a brief look.

clue.text: Stone forming capital

explanation.surface: A stone that becomes a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The state capital of Arkansas in the US; a stone is a small rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A pebble is a small rock, and the Arkansas state capital bears that name.

clue.text: Repast is, not at all oddly

definitions.text: Repast is, not at all oddly

indicators.note: not oddly says skip the odd letters and keep the even ones of the first two words

explanation.surface: A meal exists, and nothing strange about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of REPAST IS give the answer, which itself means a repast.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal food is a meal or repast.

clue.text: The part of tendering I got wrong

indicators.note: got wrong says the letters of tendering and I are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone admits they got part of a bid wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got wrong' rearranges TENDERING I.
explanation.definitionFit: A component of a recipe or mixture is one part of it.
